answers.ask: Just the one shop, or a street with the shop on it?
answers.answer: Just one small barbershop; keep the build focused inside the shop.

answers.ask: Is there a queue of customers and a score for each haircut, or is it freeform?
answers.answer: Use a simple queue of NPC customers and score each haircut, with funny results when cuts go wrong.

scene_prompt: Create a 3D game map set entirely inside one small barbershop, with a compact customer area and a barber chair/workstation as the central cutting space. Include a simple queue area for NPC customers waiting their turn, arranged clearly around the focused interior.
agent_notes: Cutting hair for a queue of NPC customers and being scored on each one is a defined, repeatable job loop, which Roleplay's own boundary note hands to Simulation as Role Sim rather than to social roleplay. I kept the Role Sim preset but replaced its world-open shape with interior-single from the wider catalogue, because the author said just one small barbershop with the build kept inside it - and for the same reason I dropped the preset's path-road-vehicle. interior-single carries no modifier and there is no outside-to-inside transition to link, so this stays P0 with no P3. Decided without a user: the queue itself is npc-population rather than a spawner, and I left physics-rig out because the comedy lives in the botched haircuts on the NPCs, not in any built contraption.
